questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Location was one of the biggest aspects when choosing a destination. I wanted to get as far away as possible.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
New Zealand is a amazing place would highly recommend.
Pro tip: buy a car it makes everything easier

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy much of what you needed was online and the rest you picked up along the way.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a orientation week but youcould also find all the info online

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: They have a housing portal online where you can apply for off campus housing. It was very stress free.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Renting housing through the host insitution was pretty expensive but good enough for a semester.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is cheaper to find something on your own but be aware of scams

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a bit of a project to get them to accept my courses, but we got there in the end. Their pre-approval process doesn’t always seem logical when it comes to which courses they accept for registration, depending on your area of study.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: As far as I remember, you apply for approval to register because you’re an exchange student, and then after that you can register. Everything happens online. But note your prefered courses have to be approved by the faculty which can take some time.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There is a student support team to assist you in the process.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: A solid 6/10. Took med about 2-3 month from start to finish to get my courses due to me insisting on getting masters courses while on the bachelor. And then when classes where about to start one of them got canceled so I had to find a new one.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early, and if they don’t want to approve your courses, talk to your head of studies and name-drop them in your emails  that should get things moving. If they really don’t want to give you your preferred courses, ask them what you should take instead; they usually comply.”

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Had a MA course that really disappointed.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had two MA courses and two BA courses

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It’s much more American-style, with midterms, and the final exam often only counts for 50% of your grade, with assignments and tests making up the rest. Lectures are either 50 minutes or two hours long, and not all courses have tutorial classes. It’s very different from UOCH, where I take two 8-week courses at a time. You have more free time, and in some cases, when the exam counts for less than 50%, you might not even need to take it.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
PAAH 101 He Tīmatanga Kōrero mō te Kori Tinana me te Hauora / Introduction to Physical Activity and Wellbeing
Is a good and fun course and you learn a lot about New Zealand history and culture. 

PHYS 412 Theoretical Physics 
Just a great course on the theory of many body quantum physics

questions.answer: public transport is super cheap, cars are also cheaper. Eating out is cheaper. And buying food is about the same.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't join any clubs but some of my friends loved it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of activities if you wanted to join.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Hiking, camping, snorkling, roadtrips. 
It's just a very beatiful country that makes you wanna be outside. It turns you into a vegetarian outdoor person.
I also did a internship with a pro football club which was setup through the host uni

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I spent almost every weedend or holiday hiking, and roadtrip'ing. Had a ski holiday which was nice and spent most of the free time exploring.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy the biggest problem was the jetlag.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk and be nice to your fellow students during class or lecture usally does the job

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: none that spring to mind

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Māori parts of the new zealand culture is a highlight giving a inside into the history of the country.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Enjoy your classes, and remember not to take studying too seriously — the real magic is in the new places you go and the friends you make along the way.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Independent living means something else in New Zealand, so if you want truly independent living, choose the Kelburn option if finding housing via the host uni.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going on holiday in the mid-term break with friends you did not know a few months earlier and making a ton of good memories

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Packing your bags and leaving the place you have called home for a semester and saying goodbye to friends who live across the world

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
Just enjoy yourself and have fun 
They only transfer the credits not the grade

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
